messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: HIGH queue/backlog for tenant 'orion-health' (VPC, dedicated pool). 95th latency > 750ms for 12m, queued requests increasing. Rule: tenant_queue_backlog > 100. Paging oncall.
laura: acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs and current config. ping @nina for customer-facing note.
laura: quick snapshot: orion-health dedicated pool: 8 GPUs, scheduler version v2.3.4, currently running global scheduler knobs plus a bespoke tenant shaper applied last month. backlog from 12 -> 220 in last 10m.
matt: looking at metrics — KV cache hit fine. Issue looks like sustained large requests + our batcher forming massive batches causing head-of-line blocking. max_batch_tokens currently 8192 for that tenant (we set it higher for throughput in peak tests).
jen: do we have any ongoing deploys to that pool? I'm seeing a canary push to runtime on two nodes 5m ago but no obvious errors.
sam: customer support (nina) says they started a heavy nightly ingestion job about 20m ago — likely correlated. they didn't expect that many concurrent short requests.
nina: can confirm. they kicked off a migration job and didn't throttle. letting them know we're investigating, they'll pause if we ask.
laura: proposed live mitigation: reduce scheduler.knobs.max_batch_tokens for tenant to 2048 and reduce max_batch_size from 128 -> 48. also enable tenant_queue_shaper with burst_capacity=200, sustain_rate=30rps. This reduces tail latency while still allowing throughput.
matt: +1. Lowering max_batch_tokens will make batches smaller and reduce head-of-line latency. Need to apply to tenant override only.
jen: any risk of reducing will spike token-cost slightly but that's ok. We should also enable immediate fallback to smaller model variant if backlog grows.
laura: patch I'm going to apply (control-plane api):

```json
PATCH /v1/tenants/orion-health/config
{
  "overrides": {
    "scheduler.knobs.max_batch_tokens": 2048,
    "scheduler.knobs.max_batch_size": 48,
    "tenant_queue_shaper": {
      "burst_capacity": 200,
      "sustain_rps": 30
    }
  }
}
```

I'll run `curl -X PATCH https://controlplane.internal/v1/tenants/orion-health/config -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" -d @patch.json` and monitor.
laura: applying patch now.
incident-bot: config-change: tenant orion-health overrides updated by laura at 1853018026
matt: seeing backlog drop from 220 -> 120 within 30s. 95th latency down to ~420ms. good sign.
jen: rolling out extra small workers to handle short requests as temporary capacity: scaling dedicated pool +2 nodes (non-disruptive). trigger: `k8s scale --replicas=10 ds/orion-worker`
laura: scaled +2, new nodes joining. backlog now 60.
nina: relayed to customer — they paused the migration job. customer appreciates the quick action.
sam: handoff: laura to matthandoff — I'm going offline in 7m. @matt please keep watch for next 30m and decide on permanent knob values.
matt: taking over. I'll keep monitoring for 45m and then we can propose a stable config for orion-health (maybe 4096 tokens + shaper tuned after x-hour load test).
laura: logging mitigation steps and root-cause notes in incident doc: reducing per-tenant max_batch_tokens to 2048 and enabling tenant_queue_shaper. Will follow up with perf regression test and cost analysis.
jen: small follow-up, we should add a guard in the scheduler: reject single-request token sizes > 120k or route them to dedicated long-request pool. Filing ticket: SCHED-948.
matt: noted. if backlog stabilizes under 50 and 95th < 500ms for 15m I'll close the pager. current metrics: backlog 42, 95th 380ms, qps steady.
laura: thanks team. nina, please keep customer informed and we'll set a post-mortem if any config change is needed for long term.
nina: will do. customer asked for a short summary they can share with infra team — I'll paste an internal blurb in #customer-success.
matt: leaving this open until 1853018120 for final check. will close after 15m stable. :white_check_mark:
